change: Restructured primary/secondary muscles. Glutes (Gluteus Maximus) moved from secondary to primary — hip drive is a prime mover in the downswing. Erector Spinae (Lower Back) moved from secondary to primary — it transfers force from lower body through the core to the hammer and resists spinal flexion throughout. Quads added as secondary stabilizers (stance/knee stability). Shoulders (Anterior Deltoids + Posterior Deltoid) moved from primary to secondary — deltoids control and decelerate/accelerate the swing but do not generate the primary power. Overall primary set: Lats, oblique, glutes, Lower Back, abs. Secondary: shoulders, forearms, Hamstrings, Quads.

Added Soleus to primary Calves entry (Gastrocnemius Lateral, Gastrocnemius Medial, Soleus) — EMG research confirms strong soleus activation during sled push propulsion alongside gastrocnemius. All other muscles and classifications unchanged.

Triceps moved from secondary to primary — in the bear crawl position the triceps brachii are continuously contracting to maintain elbow extension against body weight load and sled resistance; they are a prime mover in the upper-body portion of this exercise. Lower Back (Erector Spinae) added to secondary — isometric spinal extension holding the flat-back crawl position against the sled drag load. Calves kept as secondary. All other muscles unchanged.

Added Soleus to primary Calves entry (Gastrocnemius Lateral, Gastrocnemius Medial, Soleus) — same rationale as box sled push; soleus is strongly activated during sled push propulsion. All other muscles and classifications unchanged.

Added Soleus to primary Calves entry (Gastrocnemius Lateral, Gastrocnemius Medial, Soleus) — forward-facing sled drag with harness involves consistent calf/plantar-flexion push-off; soleus is a significant contributor alongside gastrocnemius. All other muscles and classifications unchanged.
